title: Binary search
summary: Search for target value 6 in an ascending array, comparing the midpoint element each round to rule out the half interval that cannot contain the target.
context: The input is an ascending array of 10 distinct elements indexed from 0 to 9, and the search target is target = 6; see the input table for the element at each index.

Pointers i and j mark the left and right boundaries of the current closed search interval [i, j] (both endpoints are included in the search range); m is the midpoint index of the interval, computed as (i + j) / 2 rounded down. Each round first computes the midpoint m and then compares nums[m] with the target value.
description: There are 7 frames in total: initialization followed by 3 rounds of comparison. Each round separates “computing the midpoint” from “narrowing the interval or matching the target after comparison”; the dashed box marks the current search interval.
result: Midpoint elements 12, 3, and 6 are compared in turn; the third comparison hits the target and returns index 2 rather than the element value 6.

frames.title: Initialize the search interval
frames.explanation: Set i = 0 and j = 9 so that the closed search interval [0, 9] covers all 10 elements, whose left and right endpoint values are 1 and 35, respectively; midpoint m has not yet been computed.
frames.key_state: i = 0, j = 9; closed search interval [0, 9], with no midpoint m yet.
frames.announcement: Initialize left boundary i to index 0 and right boundary j to index 9 to search the entire array.

frames.title: Round 1: compute midpoint m = 4
frames.explanation: In the closed interval [0, 9] (i = 0, j = 9), m = (0 + 9) / 2 rounded down gives 4, pointing to element 12. Next, compare it with target 6.
frames.key_state: i = 0, j = 9, m = 4; midpoint value is 12. Next, compare with target 6.
frames.announcement: Compute midpoint m at index 4, with value 12, ready to compare against target value 6.

frames.title: Round 1: 12 is greater than 6, move right boundary to 3
frames.explanation: In the previous interval [0, 9], value 12 at midpoint m = 4 is greater than target 6. Because the array is in ascending order, neither index 4 nor any index to its right can match; set j = m - 1 = 3. Now i = 0 and j = 3, giving interval [0, 3] with remaining elements [1, 3, 6, 8]; the old pointer m still points to index 4 (value 12) outside the interval and has not yet been recomputed.
frames.key_state: Because value 12 at m = 4 is greater than target 6, the interval narrows from [0, 9] to [0, 3]: i = 0, j = 3, remaining [1, 3, 6, 8]; old m = 4 remains outside the interval.
frames.announcement: Midpoint value 12 is greater than target value 6, so right boundary j moves to index 3, keeping indices 0 through 3.

frames.title: Round 2: compute midpoint m = 1
frames.explanation: In the closed interval [0, 3] (i = 0, j = 3), m = (0 + 3) / 2 rounded down gives 1, pointing to element 3. Next, compare it with target 6.
frames.key_state: i = 0, j = 3, m = 1; midpoint value is 3. Next, compare with target 6.
frames.announcement: Within interval [0, 3], recompute midpoint m at index 1, with value 3.

frames.title: Round 2: 3 is less than 6, move left boundary to 2
frames.explanation: In the previous interval [0, 3], value 3 at midpoint m = 1 is less than target 6. Because the array is in ascending order, neither index 1 nor any index to its left can match; set i = m + 1 = 2. Now i = 2 and j = 3, giving interval [2, 3] with remaining elements [6, 8]; the old pointer m still points to index 1 (value 3) outside the interval and has not yet been recomputed.
frames.key_state: Because value 3 at m = 1 is less than target 6, the interval narrows from [0, 3] to [2, 3]: i = 2, j = 3, remaining [6, 8]; old m = 1 remains outside the interval.
frames.announcement: Midpoint value 3 is less than target value 6, so left boundary i moves to index 2, leaving only 6 and 8 in the interval.

frames.title: Round 3: compute midpoint m = 2
frames.explanation: In the closed interval [2, 3] (i = 2, j = 3), m = (2 + 3) / 2 rounded down gives 2, coinciding with left boundary i and pointing to element 6. Next, compare it with target 6.
frames.key_state: i and m coincide at index 2, j = 3; midpoint value is 6. Next, compare with target 6.
frames.announcement: Recompute midpoint m at index 2, coinciding with left boundary i, with value 6.

frames.title: Round 3: target found, return index 2
frames.explanation: Value 6 at midpoint m = 2 equals target 6, ending the search. The final frame keeps only midpoint pointer m pointing to index 2, while boundary pointers i and j and the dashed interval box are hidden.
frames.key_state: Target value 6 found; only m = 2 is shown, returning index 2.
frames.announcement: The midpoint value equals target value 6; the search succeeds and returns index 2.
